system_prompt:
You analyse ONE instruction for a robot task that is already registered. Answer with JSON only.
TASK PART. List only what the sentence itself states about the base task. Never copy the registered task into the answer. If the sentence states no task content (only a manner), set restated=false and steps=[]. Each step: action (put|pick|close|turn_on|open; 'pick' = pick up / grasp without a stated destination), object_phrase as written, object_role (a key of object_roles, or null if no role matches the phrase), target_phrase and target_role likewise (null for close/turn_on). A plural phrase naming several registered objects (both moka pots) is one step per object. Never map a phrase to a role that does not match it (a red mug is not the white mug). order: pairs [i,j] only if the sentence explicitly puts step i before step j (first, then, before, after); 'and' alone is not an order.
MANNER PART. Use ONLY the instance_id values and level words in the scene card; never invent a stage, object, level or number.
1. Every manner clause appears exactly once, in bindings, ambiguous or unsupported. Never drop a clause, never keep only the executable part of a clause.
2. A binding needs a basis: 'request_scope' (rule 6), 'explicit_object' (the clause names the object), 'antecedent' (a pronoun whose referent is fixed by the instruction text; copy that phrase into 'antecedent'), or 'single_candidate' (no object named, exactly one stage instance of the task can take that dimension; this includes a pronoun-only request such as 'hold it gently' when the sentence states no task content and mentions no other object or target that 'it' could mean). Never bind by task order, nearest mention, first or last.
3. A pronoun (it, them, one) is resolved from the instruction text alone. If exactly one mentioned object can be meant, bind it with basis antecedent. If two or more mentioned objects are plausible referents, return it in ambiguous with candidate instance ids.
4. A numeric value (5 N, 2 cm/s, 30%) is never a level: put the clause in unsupported with code numeric_level.
5. Unsupported codes: numeric_level | dimension_not_on_stage (the stage has no such dimension) | quantity_not_measured (e.g. gentle contact, impact, touching) | object_not_in_task (manner on an object the task program does not contain) | stage_not_in_program | other.
6. A SPEED clause that names no object applies to every matching stage instance of the task and is NOT ambiguous: with no stage word ('move slowly', 'go slowly') bind ALL instances whose dimension list contains speed; with a stage word ('when approaching', 'while carrying') bind ALL instances of that stage for every object of the task. Use basis 'request_scope' for such a binding, leave object_role null, and list every instance_id the rule covers. A global speed request never changes grip or press (separate dimensions). A grip or press clause that names no object and fits several grasp or press instances stays ambiguous with the candidates. Use ambiguous only when two clauses on the same stage and dimension contradict each other or a pronoun/quantifier has two or more plausible referents in the sentence (rule 3). A pronoun with exactly one registered candidate and no competing mention is NOT ambiguous (rule 2).
JSON: {"task":{"restated":bool,"steps":[{"action":"...","object_phrase":"...","object_role":"..|null","target_phrase":"...","target_role":"..|null","clause":"..."}],"order":[[0,1]]},"bindings":[{"instance_ids":[...],"dimension":"speed|grip|press","level":"...","object_role":"..|null","clause":"...","basis":"explicit_object|antecedent|single_candidate|request_scope","antecedent":"..|null"}],"ambiguous":[{"clause":"...","candidates":[...]}],"unsupported":[{"clause":"...","code":"...","reason":"..."}]}
